evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/faults.tsx:444-458 - FaultDetailPageRoute wires every state-changing fault action as a bare fire-and-forget mutation with NO error handling: onTriage -> triage.mutate({priority,category,assigned_to}) (:445), onResolve -> resolve.mutate({resolution_notes}) (:451), onConfirm -> confirm.mutate(rating) (:452), onReopen -> reopen.mutate(reason) (:453), onAddComment -> addComment.mutate(...) (:455), onAddAttachment -> addAttachment.mutate(file) (:457), onDeleteAttachment -> deleteAttachment.mutate(id) (:458). None passes an onError option and none is wrapped in try/catch.

The mutation hooks come from @ppt/api-client (faults.tsx:14-29 import block) and are generated with ONLY an onSuccess handler and NO onError: frontend/packages/api-client/src/faults/hooks.ts:182-192 useResolveFault (useMutation with mutationFn + onSuccess invalidateQueries, no onError), :195-205 useConfirmFault (same shape), :208+ useReopenFault (same shape), and the sibling useTriageFault/useAddComment/useAddAttachment/useDeleteAttachment follow the identical generated pattern. TanStack Query therefore swallows a rejected mutationFn: the promise rejection is captured internally and, with no onError anywhere, produces zero UI feedback.

Net effect: a manager clicking Resolve / Triage / Reopen on a fault whose request 4xx/5xx (permission denied, validation error, server error) sees NOTHING - no toast, no inline error, no state change - and reasonably believes the action succeeded (the cache is not invalidated on failure either, so the stale status persists on screen). This is a correctness/UX defect on manager-critical fault-workflow transitions.

The gap is inconsistent within the SAME route wrapper: the fault-DETAIL QUERY error IS surfaced - faults.tsx:407-415 runs a useEffect that shows an error toast when the useFault query `error` is set. Only the mutations are unhandled. The correct mutation pattern already exists elsewhere in the segment (routes/groups/reports.tsx:148-157 downloadReport.mutate(id,{onError:()=>showToast(...)}), guarded by a regression test reports.download-retry.route.test.tsx; and routes/groups/financial.tsx:204-210 defines onError inline on its mutations).

This is NET-NEW vs prior ppt-web-core signals: the already-filed faults findings were code-review-ppt-web-core-faults-url-param-unvalidated-cast (2026-09-11, URL enum cast) and the auth-guard findings (2026-09-17/09-20); the already-filed silent-error finding code-review-ppt-web-core-financial-query-silent-error (2026-09-17) covers financial QUERIES (isError not read), a different file and a different mechanism (query vs mutation). No prior signal covers the fault-detail mutation onError gap.

Fix (low-risk): pass an onError toast at each call site in faults.tsx (mirroring reports.tsx), or add a shared onError to the generated fault mutation hooks. Confidence high: full call path traced from the FaultDetailPage handler props through the generated hook definitions confirming no onError exists at either layer; reachable in production on the /faults/:faultId manager route.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/OrganizationProvider.tsx:8-10 - the context value is rebuilt as a fresh object literal on every render: `const value = user?.organizationId ? { organizationId: user.organizationId, organizationName: user.organizationName } : null;` then passed straight to <OrganizationContext.Provider value={value}>. It is not wrapped in useMemo.

OrganizationProvider consumes useAuth() (:6) and re-renders whenever the AuthContext value changes (e.g. every silent token refresh calls setUser with a spread-new user object - contexts/AuthContext.tsx:433-435 - so AuthContext re-renders are frequent). Each such render yields a new `value` object identity even when organizationId/organizationName are unchanged, so every component subscribed via useOrganization() re-renders unnecessarily.

Impact is a performance/correctness-of-render smell rather than a crash: consumers relying on referential stability of the org context (memoized selectors, effect deps keyed on the context object) will re-run on unrelated auth churn. Low severity; the fix is to wrap the object in useMemo([user?.organizationId, user?.organizationName]). Net-new: no prior ppt-web-core signal covers OrganizationProvider. Confidence medium (static-only; not runtime-profiled).
